# v1.1.0-dev.121: Splitters that let go, windows that come back

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.120`.

## Splitter bars unhover honestly

The drag bars between panes used to stay lit after the cursor crossed
onto a docked window: that window takes every pointer event from there,
so the bar never heard the mouse leave. Hover is now driven by the app
itself and ends the moment the cursor is off the bar, docked window or
not.

## The group that comes forward gets a working keyboard

Clicking a virtual window's taskbar button, or alt-tabbing onto the
container itself, brought the group forward with a dead keyboard: the
container is deliberately not focusable, and nothing handed the
keyboard on to the window you were last using inside it. Now one does.

## No undock path can strand a window at its pane size

Closing a virtual window, a Load releasing a member, a pane leaving the
layout, a placement that failed on a hung app, and quitting while a
member's app refused to close: any of these could release a docked
window without handing back the size it arrived with, leaving it
permanently reshaped. Every one of them restores it now. A quit can no
longer leave a fully docked window stranded at its dock rectangle, a
crash mid-undock now leaves a state the next Load recovers instead of a
window the app can no longer see, and a hard kill of WLM no longer
leaves the windows of a hidden container invisible with no taskbar
button and no way back.

## Smaller

A one-time failure talking to the taskbar no longer disables taskbar
handling for the whole session. The repo also gained a full greenfield
document series under `docs/greenfield/`: the product, user and
platform research, a complete technical design, a phased build plan,
the edge-case bible, and a build guide for an AI harness.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
